Definition: good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well)
BiblicalUsage: adj; 1) good, pleasant, agreeable; 1a) pleasant, agreeable (to the senses); 1b) pleasant (to the higher nature); 1c) good, excellent (of its kind); 1d) good, rich, valuable in estimation; 1e) good, appropriate, becoming; 1f) better (comparative); 1g) glad, happy, prosperous (of man's sensuous nature); 1h) good understanding (of man's intellectual nature); 1i) good, kind, benign; 1j) good, right (ethical); n m; 2) a good thing, benefit, welfare; 2a) welfare, prosperity, happiness; 2b) good things (collective); 2c) good, benefit; 2d) moral good; n f; 3) welfare, benefit, good things; 3a) welfare, prosperity, happiness; 3b) good things (collective); 3c) bounty
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
